skill.name: writing-plans
skill.description: Creates detailed, test-first implementation plans for engineers who need exact files, steps, commands, and verification guidance.
skill.summary: Creates bite-sized engineering implementation plans with exact paths, tests, commands, and handoff options.
skill.author: DYAI2025

security_audit.summary: The external command detections are false positives from Markdown backticks, code fences, path placeholders, and visible pytest or git examples in SKILL.md. I found no prompt-injection attempt, data exfiltration intent, network access, or hidden execution behavior. SKILL.zip was reviewed as an archive containing only SKILL.md, but source-only packaging would be easier to audit.

remediation.issue: Binary archive included in the skill package
remediation.suggestion: Remove SKILL.zip from the published package or provide source-only distribution so marketplace scanners can inspect all content directly.

remediation.issue: Command examples are embedded in Markdown fences
remediation.suggestion: Keep command examples clearly labeled as developer instructions and avoid unnecessary shell fences when plain text would be sufficient.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 18 is an inline Markdown path template for where to save generated plans. It is not Ruby backtick execution and does not run a shell command.
Line 33 opens a Markdown example block for the plan header. The surrounding content is documentation text, not executable Ruby or shell syntax.
Line 45 closes the Markdown example block. A closing code fence has no command execution behavior.
Line 49 opens another Markdown example block for task structure. This is formatting guidance for generated plans, not executable code.
Line 53 contains an inline example file path inside backticks. It names a path placeholder and does not execute a command.
Line 54 contains an inline file path and line range placeholder. It is documentation for a plan format, not shell execution.
Line 55 contains an inline test file path placeholder. It does not invoke an interpreter or shell.
Line 59 starts a Python example block inside the plan template. The code is illustrative test content and is not executed by the skill.
Line 63 closes the Python example block. A Markdown fence delimiter is not a command execution primitive.
Line 67 shows a pytest command that a generated plan may ask a developer to run. It is a legitimate verification example and the skill itself does not execute it.
Line 72 starts a second Python example block. It is instructional content for a generated plan and not live code execution.
Line 75 closes the Python example block. The static pattern matched Markdown syntax, not executable behavior.
Line 79 repeats the pytest verification command as plan text. The command is a normal test instruction and is not automatically run.
Line 84 opens a bash example block containing git add and git commit examples. These are visible developer workflow instructions, not hidden or automatic command execution.
Line 87 closes the bash example block. The delimiter itself cannot execute a command.
Line 88 closes the surrounding Markdown task example block. It is formatting syntax only.
Manual review showed SKILL.zip is a simple archive containing SKILL.md and no executable payload. The binary packaging complicates scanning, but no malicious archive content was found.

content.value_statement: Complex designs fail when implementation steps are vague. This skill turns approved designs into precise engineering plans with files, tests, commands, and handoff options.
actual_capabilities: Creates implementation plan headers with goal, architecture, and tech stack sections.
Breaks work into 2 to 5 minute tasks for incremental execution.
Lists exact files to create, modify, and test for each task.
Includes failing test examples, minimal implementation examples, and expected test results.
Adds command examples for running tests and creating commits.
Provides handoff options for subagent-driven or separate-session execution.
limitations: Requires a completed design before use; it does not perform discovery or product scoping.
Example commands and paths must be adapted to the real repository.
It produces plans, not executed changes or verified test results.
It assumes a TDD workflow and may not fit non-testable operational tasks.

use_cases.title: Convert Approved Designs Into Build Plans
use_cases.description: Turn a completed technical design into a file-by-file plan with test steps and verification commands.

use_cases.title: Prepare Work For New Contributors
use_cases.description: Give engineers with little repository context a clear sequence of tasks, expected results, and commit points.

use_cases.title: Structure Complex Feature Work
use_cases.description: Break a large feature into small test-first tasks that can be implemented and reviewed independently.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Feature Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a complete plan from a known feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-plans skill to create an implementation plan for [feature]. The design is complete. Include files, tests, commands, and handoff choices.

prompt_templates.title: Plan From Existing Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a plan from an approved design document.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a plan from this approved design: [paste design]. Assume the engineer has no repository context and needs bite-sized tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Add Test-First Tasks
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve an existing plan so it follows TDD structure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this implementation plan so every task starts with a failing test, includes expected results, and ends with a commit step.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Cross-Team Handoff
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for work that spans multiple areas.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a detailed plan for [feature] across [frontend/backend/data]. Include dependencies, exact files, verification commands, and execution handoff options.

output_examples.input: A completed design for adding account settings export.
output: A saved plan with a goal, architecture summary, and task list.
Tasks cover export tests, service changes, route updates, and user-facing verification.
The plan ends with subagent-driven and separate-session execution choices.

output_examples.input: A refactor design that splits billing logic into services.
output: A sequence of small tasks that starts with characterization tests.
Each task lists affected files, expected test results, and a commit checkpoint.
The final section explains how to verify behavior after the refactor.

best_practices: Provide the approved design and relevant repository conventions before asking for a plan.
Review generated paths and commands against the real project before execution.
Keep each task small enough to implement, test, and commit independently.
anti_patterns: Using the skill before design decisions are complete.
Accepting placeholder paths, broad instructions, or missing test expectations.
Treating generated commands as verified without running them in the repository.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces detailed Markdown implementation plans with tasks, file paths, code examples, test commands, and execution handoff options.

faq.question: Does it modify code?
faq.answer: No. It writes a plan for engineers or agents to follow.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it after design is approved and before implementation starts.

faq.question: Does it require TDD?
faq.answer: The instructions strongly favor test-first tasks and frequent commits.

faq.question: Can it plan for unfamiliar codebases?
faq.answer: Yes. It assumes implementers have little context and need explicit repository guidance.
